items.detail: Sandra's Xi'an standout, and the right thing to do on a jet-lagged first afternoon because it asks nothing of you but pedalling. ¥45 for three hours then ¥5 per extra ten minutes; deposit ¥200. Six rental stations, 13.7 km around, two to three hours. Return to any station until 20:00; after that everything goes back to South Gate (永宁门), open until 22:00, evening returns by 21:30. Check both brakes before you ride off — hers had one.
items.name: Ming city wall bike ride

items.detail: The other easy win, a short walk from the wall's north side.
items.name: Muslim Quarter after dark

items.detail: Three pits, still being excavated, nothing air-conditioned — which matters far less in October than it did in Sandra's July. ¥120, 08:30–17:00, so it's a morning start. Pit 2 has been half-closed for works since 5 September under a notice running about a month.
items.name: Terracotta Warriors

items.detail: North square, five minutes' walk from the Westin. Good for an evening with nothing left in you.
items.name: Big Wild Goose Pagoda fountain show

items.detail: The fallback if the Shaanxi History Museum release fails: free, quiet and never sell out.
items.name: Small Wild Goose Pagoda & Xi'an Museum

items.detail: Sandra fell for this one. The tell is someone asking you to take a photo OF THEM — locals who approach Westerners want to be in the picture. If a friendly stranger steers the conversation toward tea, walk away mid-sentence.
items.name: The tea ceremony scam

items.detail:
Top of Sandra's ranking. Closed for a long renovation after her visit and reopened in 2022 — free, 09:00–17:00, last entry 16:00, shut WEDNESDAYS. Booking opens seven days out, so Sunday the 11th means 4 October, while you are between Shigatse and Lhasa.

NOT FATAL IF YOU MISS THE SLOT: there are reservation machines in the lobby and it generally takes walk-ins off-peak, which a post-Golden-Week Sunday very much is.
items.name: Urban Planning Exhibition Center

items.detail: No longer the apartment-block basement Sandra found — moved in 2019 to the seventh floor of 726 Yan'an West Road. ¥25, 10:00–17:00, still barely signposted, opens daily. Nine-minute walk from Jiangsu Road, which is on your own Line 11.
items.name: Propaganda Poster Art Centre

items.detail: The Bund for the Art Deco and the live jazz; Yu Gardens and the bird-and-cricket market if there's daylight left. Skip the Railway Museum.
items.name: The Bund, then Yu Gardens

items.detail:
The Art Deco landmark on the Bund has run an old-timers' jazz band in its bar for decades, and you do not need to be a guest to sit in.

IT COSTS YOU THE EARLY NIGHT. The Sunday plan has you leaving the Bund about 18:45 for Toy Story, 45 minutes away, with Monday being your first park day and rope drop the whole game. Check-in runs to 06:00 so it is possible — just know what you are trading.
items.name: Jazz at the Fairmont Peace Hotel

items.detail: China's first state-run contemporary art museum, in a converted riverside power station — the building is most of the appeal. The substitute if the Urban Planning Center booking fails or Yu Gardens sounds like too much walking. Check hours in the app on the day.
items.name: Power Station of Art

items.detail: Shikumen lane-house alleys turned over to small studios and cafes. More interesting than Xintiandi, which is the polished version of the same idea a few blocks away. No booking, no fixed hours to miss — the useful filler if the Sunday runs ahead of schedule.
items.name: Tianzifang

items.detail:
Sandra's one clear dud in Shanghai. Named here so it does not get rediscovered as an idea on the day.

NOT THE SAME PLACE as the Shanghai Metro Museum out at Ziteng Road, which is on the Sunday plan and is a different museum entirely.
items.name: Skip the Shanghai Railway Museum
